extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH grant applications and peer reviewers evaluating the Vertebrate Animals Section (VAS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reviewer criteria for the Vertebrate Animals Section (VAS) of NIH grant applications, specifying required content, justifications, and oversight for use of live vertebrate animals. Used by applicants to prepare the VAS and by reviewers to evaluate adequacy and appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Procedures Involving Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Must include species, strains, ages, sex, total number of animals to be used, and a concise description of the proposed procedures involving live vertebrate animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine procedures (housing, husbandry) generally not required to be described. Provide concise but specific procedural description sufficient for reviewer assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justifications for Use of Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the chosen species and strain are appropriate for the proposed research and why the research goals cannot be accomplished using alternative models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives to address: computational models, human studies, invertebrate models, in vitro / cell culture, and existing data/biospecimens. Also justify the appropriateness of the species and the number of animals (minimum needed for valid statistical conclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions to Minimize Discomfort, Distress, Pain, and Injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe interventions to limit animal pain and distress during the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include description of analgesia, anesthesia, sedation; palliative care; methods of restraint; surgical procedures; plan for monitoring animals during and after procedures; and humane endpoints (criteria for early removal from study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for Method of Euthanasia
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification for the method of euthanasia when it is not consistent with the AVMA Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using an AVMA-consistent method, a simple statement that it is AVMA-consistent is sufficient. If using an alternative method, provide a scientific justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Standard — Unacceptable Rating
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will be rated UNACCEPTABLE if all required items are not addressed adequately or are found inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must determine adequacy and appropriateness of required VAS items; omission or inappropriate responses can render the VAS (and application) unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: IACUC Approval Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) approval is required before NIH funds can be released and animals must be procured from approved sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal care must follow the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals. Ensure IACUC approval is in place prior to award/funds release and that procurement and care comply with institutional and federal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: OLAW Animal Welfare Assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Performing institution must have an Animal Welfare Assurance approved by NIH's Office of Laboratory Animal Welfare (OLAW).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution must also have an IACUC composition meeting federal requirements; maintain institutional assurances and compliance with OLAW policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worksheet for Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH provides a Vertebrate Animal Section worksheet to standardize reviewer evaluation across the four criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should use the VAS worksheet to ensure consistent assessment of Description of Procedures, Justifications, Interventions to minimize pain, and Euthanasia justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Consideration — Field Studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Field studies involving vertebrate animals carry additional reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants conducting field research must address those extra reporting elements (permit information, site-specific considerations, methods appropriate for field conditions) as required by NIH guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Consideration — Endangered Species
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies using endangered species require permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required permits are obtained and described; provide justification and compliance documentation as part of the VAS when endangered species are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Consideration — Non-human Primates
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies using non-human primates receive heightened review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect additional scrutiny and justification for use, numbers, procedures, and welfare protections when proposing work with non-human primates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Consideration — USDA-regulated Species
rubrics_metrics.description: USDA-regulated species (most mammals) have additional oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must account for USDA regulatory requirements and oversight in their planning and documentation; provide relevant compliance details in the VAS.
